model.name: Drawer pan/zoom: full mouse parity (touch-first)
model.description: The drawer pan/zoom is touch-first (touch is the primary design surface) but MUST work identically with a mouse: mouse-drag pans (mirrors 1-finger pan), scroll-wheel zooms (mirrors pinch-zoom), and double-click resets/toggles (mirrors double-tap). Mouse mirrors the touch behaviour exactly.
model.tronQuote: > TRON: "the drawer works well on touch and it shall be touch first, but it shall also work the same way with mouse."

acceptanceCriteria.text: Touch remains the primary surface: 1-finger drag pans, pinch zooms, double-tap resets/toggles (unchanged).
Mouse-drag pans the drawer content, identical to 1-finger pan.
Scroll-wheel zooms the drawer content, identical to pinch-zoom (zoom toward the pointer).
Double-click resets/toggles the zoom, identical to double-tap.
Behaviour is identical across input types — no mouse-only or touch-only divergence in pan/zoom/reset.
Verified live (headless) on both a touch surface and a mouse/pointer surface.

model.crossRefNote: Extends the R21.9 rb-preview-pane / RbPanZoom pan/zoom surface with full mouse parity.
model.coverageNote: 2026-06-30 triage: the grab-bar-mouse + X-minimize bugs moved to a DEDICATED requirement R25.4 (225b18a6, sibling) per architect diagnosis + PO. The AC-grab I briefly added here was BACKED OUT to keep single-source - R22.2 stays scoped to drawer pan/zoom CONTENT mouse-parity; R25.4 owns grab-bar drag + X-minimize.
model.refinedByNote: R25.4 extends the R22.2 touch-first mouse-parity PRINCIPLE to the drawer chrome (grab-bar drag + X-minimize), which R22.2's content pan/zoom ACs did not cover.
